Apply Now

  • Help shape resilient water services for the Wellington region
  • Influence lifecycle planning, condition assessment and capital investment priorities

About the Role

This is a senior asset planning and people leadership opportunity with a major Wellington region water services provider.

You’ll lead a specialist team focused on treatment facilities and bulk water assets, turning condition, performance, resilience and regulatory insights into clear investment priorities.

This is a role for an experienced water infrastructure planning professional who wants to influence long-term decisions, support reliable services, and contribute to infrastructure that communities depend on every day.

Based in Petone, this is a full-time permanent role offering highly competitive remuneration, aligned to the seniority, leadership scope and technical influence of the position.

You will:

  • Lead strategic asset planning for treatment facilities and the bulk water network
  • Lead condition assessment frameworks and annual inspection planning
  • Influence lifecycle planning and capital investment priorities
  • Support capital project scoping as the planning representative
  • Lead, coach and develop a small technical team
  • Build a high-performing, collaborative and accountable team culture

About You

You’ll bring strong water infrastructure planning experience, technical credibility and the confidence to lead people through complex planning, prioritisation and decision-making.

You are likely to have:

  • A Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Civil, Environmental or Process Engineering
  • Around 10+ years’ experience in water infrastructure planning
  • At least 3+ years’ experience leading people or technical teams
  • Strong knowledge of water supply, wastewater treatment, drainage systems and asset lifecycle planning
  • Understanding of regulatory frameworks, risk-based planning and long-term infrastructure investment
  • Confidence working with condition assessment data, asset health insights and capital planning processes
  • Strong stakeholder engagement, written reporting and presentation skills
  • A collaborative leadership style with the ability to coach and motivate technical specialists

What’s on Offer

This is a visible leadership role where your work will directly influence the future of essential water infrastructure across the Wellington region.

  • Flexible working arrangements, including up to two days working from home

job.title: Senior Commissioning Engineer – Water & Wastewater Treatment
job.description:
• Shape best-practice commissioning across a major water infrastructure environment
  • High-impact role ensuring assets are truly operational before handover
  • Senior technical advisory role across water and wastewater treatment

Shape the future of critical water infrastructure

Our client is seeking an experienced Senior Commissioning Engineer - Water & Wastewater Treatment to provide technical leadership across the commissioning and handover of new and upgraded treatment facilities.

This is a senior role focused on treatment plant systems - mechanical, electrical, instrumentation, controls and process performance. You will act as a subject matter expert for commissioning quality, helping ensure assets are safe, reliable and fully operational before being handed over to operations.

This is an opportunity to influence how commissioning is approached across a significant infrastructure portfolio. If you are passionate about operational readiness, technical excellence and leaving a legacy of well-commissioned infrastructure, this role offers both challenge and purpose.

About the role

This is not a hands-on site commissioning role. It is a senior technical and advisory position focused on governance, assurance, quality and operational performance.

The role is primarily focused on commissioning treatment plant systems, including:

  • Water and wastewater treatment plants
  • Mechanical and electrical systems
  • Instrumentation, controls and SCADA
  • Process plant upgrades and new facilities

As a senior technical advisor, you will:

  • Provide technical leadership for the commissioning and handover of water and wastewater treatment plant projects
  • Review and approve commissioning plans, methodologies and data deliverables
  • Ensure operational readiness and asset performance prior to handover
  • Champion best-practice commissioning standards across the project lifecycle
  • Work closely with operations, digital, planning and project teams
  • Act as a technical advisor and mentor to project teams and junior engineers

About you

You are a technically credible commissioning engineer with strong treatment plant experience and the ability to influence project teams and operational stakeholders.

You will bring:

  • Commissioning experience on water or wastewater treatment plants, ideally across mechanical, electrical, process or controls systems
  • Strong understanding of operational readiness, asset handover and plant performance
  • Experience working with contractors, system integrators and operational teams
  • The ability to provide technical leadership, mentor others and drive best practice
  • Excellent stakeholder engagement and communication skills

Ideally, you will have:

  • A background in Mechanical, Electrical, Process or Controls Engineering
  • A minimum of seven years’ post-qualification experience in water or wastewater treatment infrastructure
  • Chartered Professional Engineer (CPEng) status or be working towards it

The opportunity

You’ll join a collaborative, values-driven organisation responsible for critical water infrastructure and work across complex, meaningful projects that serve communities for generations.

The role offers:

  • A supportive and professional engineering environment
  • High-impact projects across water and wastewater treatment plants
  • Flexible working options and strong professional development support
  • The opportunity to shape commissioning standards and future capability

How to Apply

Click ‘Apply’ or, to find out more, contact Fiona Clarke on 027 688 8837. Your application will be received in confidence.

Peak Recruitment is managing the recruitment of this position on behalf of our client. Please direct all enquiries and applications to Peak Recruitment.

job.title: Structural Engineer – Steel Buildings
job.description:
Employer: Donovan Group
  • Design structural steel buildings from analysis through to fabrication
  • Work alongside experienced CPEng engineers and build your pathway to chartership
  • Join an innovative NZ business combining engineering, technology and manufacturing
About the Role
Peak Recruitment is partnering with Donovan Group to find a Structural Engineer for its Whangārei-based structural team.
Working alongside highly experienced structural engineers, you will:
  • Complete structural analysis and calculations for steel buildings
  • Develop and maintain structural models using SAP2000
  • Prepare calculation packs for internal review and building consent
  • Design and refine structural steel components and connections
  • Work closely with detailers, architects, clients and other engineers
  • Gain direct exposure to fabrication and buildability
  • Contribute to design optimisation, automation and engineering improvements
  • Take on increasing technical and project responsibility as your experience grows
This is a full-time, permanent position with a competitive salary depending on skills and experience.

About You

You will ideally have:
  • A bachelor’s degree in Structural or Civil Engineering
  • 1–5 years’ structural engineering experience
  • Hands-on experience analysing or designing steel structures or steel buildings
  • Experience using SAP2000, ETABS, Multiframe or similar structural analysis software
  • Knowledge of relevant New Zealand structural and steel design standards
  • Strong analytical skills and attention to detail
  • Excellent communication skills and a practical, collaborative approach
Most importantly, we want to hear about the steel structures you have personally worked on.

Why Donovan Group?

Donovan Group brings together engineering, technology and manufacturing to deliver steel building systems across New Zealand through brands including Coresteel and KiwiSpan.

You will work closely with experienced engineers, detailers and the manufacturing team, giving you practical insight into how structural decisions influence fabrication, cost, efficiency and buildability across commercial and industrial steel-building projects.

You will also be supported to develop toward CPEng, contribute to innovation and automation initiatives, and take on greater technical and project responsibility as your capability grows.

How to Apply

Click ‘Apply’ and upload your CV and application letter or to find out more, contact Fiona Clarke on 027 688 8837.  Applications close 6 September 2026 or when the vacancy is filled so we encourage you to apply promptly. Your application will be received in confidence.

With Mount Taranaki on your doorstep, world-class surf beaches, mountain biking, a vibrant arts scene and an enviable work-life balance, Taranaki offers an exceptional place to build both your career and your lifestyle.  If you're considering a move to New Zealand, we'd love to hear from you. International applications are welcome with visa and residency pathways available for eligible candidates.

The Opportunity

Reporting to the Three Waters Planning Lead, you'll help plan the future of New Plymouth's drinking-water infrastructure.  This is a strategic planning role where you'll combine technical expertise with long-term thinking to influence infrastructure investment and deliver sustainable water supply outcomes.

You’ll work across:
  • strategic planning for water supply sources, treatment and distribution;
  • growth and capacity planning supported by network modelling;
  • asset management and long-term investment planning;
  • business case development;
  • project leadership, consultant management and technical oversight; and
  • stakeholder engagement across the organisation and wider community.
About You

You're an experienced planning engineer with a strong understanding of water-supply systems and a passion for solving complex infrastructure challenges.

You’ll have a tertiary qualification in civil, environmental or water engineering (or a related discipline), together with 7+ years' relevant experience in water infrastructure engineering, including hydraulic modelling (ideally with Infoworks WS Pro) and design.

A strategic thinker by nature, you look beyond individual projects to consider the wider network, future growth, resilience, and community outcomes.  You have a knack for translating technical insights into clear, practical direction.

Strong communication and relationship-building skills enable you to engage confidently with both technical and non-technical audiences across the organisation and wider community.

Why Join Us?

If you're looking to apply your technical expertise at a strategic level, this is an opportunity to work asset-owner side and influence the planning and investment decisions that will shape the future of water services for generations to come. You'll be joining a collaborative, supportive team where your expertise is respected, your ideas are valued and your work makes a tangible difference. Combined with flexible working and ongoing professional development, it's an opportunity to build a rewarding long-term career in one of New Zealand's most desirable regions.

Across New Zealand, significant investment and reform are creating exciting opportunities for experienced water professionals. You'll join New Plymouth District Council's Water Planning team, playing a key role as water services transition to Wai Hononga Water Services Ltd.

Ready to Shape the Future?

Whether you're already in New Zealand or considering relocating, we'd love to hear from you. Visa sponsorship and relocation assistance may be available for the preferred candidate.

This is a full-time permanent position with a starting salary in the range of NZD $117,000 to $130,000 depending on experience and qualifications.

Click ‘Apply’ or to find out more, contact Fiona Clarke on 027 688 8837. Applications close 23 August 2026 or when the vacancy is filled so we encourage you to apply promptly. Your application will be received in confidence. 

New Plymouth District Council has engaged Peak Recruitment to manage the recruitment of this position. Please direct all enquiries and applications to Peak Recruitment.
